reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis that a magnetic rare-earth addition (Tb) degrades superconductivity by introducing magnetic scattering centers and nonsuperconducting inclusions is well-grounded in established superconductor physics and known effects of magnetic impurities on superconductivity.
reasons.testability: A direct comparison of Tb-doped and undoped alloys under identical conditions, with measurable criteria (Tc shift, Hc2 reduction, transition broadening), and clear pass/fail outcomes makes the hypothesis test straightforward and decisive.
reasons.usefulness: This approach addresses a novel composition in high-entropy superconductors, providing both a mechanistic rationale and a clear experimental plan that could guide further optimization or avoidance of magnetic dopants.
